1.why: A and D are both real senses of 'temperate' and only the source can choose between climate and conduct; B ('slow to reach a verdict') and C ('lukewarm in enthusiasm') are senses of 'deliberate' and 'tepid' respectively, not of 'temperate', so no context could make them the definition.

2.why: A (climate), B (abstinence) and C (measured) are all genuine senses of 'temperate' and only the source picks among them; D 'lukewarm' is the sense of 'tepid', not 'temperate', so it cannot be the definition under any context.

3.why: Only B concedes the finding and then qualifies its mechanism; A, C and D are absolutes ('every additional hour reliably', 'any ground', 'instead be made shorter'), the standard distractor cast around a hedged key, but each remains arguable to a source-holder.

4.why: All four are coherent functions for a middle paragraph and nothing in the option set alone rules any out; D is chosen only because a shift from description to argument is the commonest work for the paragraph before a closing one.

5.why: The stem asks for structure and only C names a structural sequence (state a reading, reinterpret its evidence, invert it); A, B and D state critical positions rather than shapes, but a source-holder could still argue any of them describes the passage.

6.why: A is Rousseau's own general-will formulation; B is the might-makes-right position Rousseau explicitly refutes and D is the majority-imposition reading his general will is defined against, so neither can be what a passage on Rousseau supports; C is a substantive claim the source could carry.

7.why: B is illegal because a passage generating this stem must treat neuroplasticity as bearing on recovery, so 'no role' contradicts its premise; among the rest D is the only bounded answer, while A rests on the absolute 'any circuit'.

8.why: D is the only option describing a two-move structure (grant, then qualify) as the stem demands; A, B and C assert content positions, though a source-holder could argue for any of them.

9.why: D is the only option carrying a specific reversal (the supposed drawback turns out to be an advantage), the shape an item is written to test; A, B and C are generic structure templates that remain legal without the source.

10.why: B is illegal: no text asserts phlogiston was 'ultimately correct and ought never to have been abandoned'. Between the survivors C is the only one that both credits the old theory and marks its failure, while A names a narrow chemical mechanism and D an unqualified triumph.

11.why: Four plausible descriptions of a document type with nothing in the set to exclude any; B chosen only as the most specific of the four.

12.why: The idiom 'a wash' has a fixed meaning, break-even, so A (small), B (routine) and D (formality) are things a break-even outcome might also be but are not what the phrase means, and no context can redefine a set idiom.

13.why: All four are arguable skeptic replies with the source hidden; D is chosen because it is the only one that weighs the two evidence classes against each other, which is what the stem's 'together' invites.

14.why: B is illegal because both texts, to be paired at all, take the end-of-period die-off as a mass extinction and dispute its cause; C is the only option in which the two texts differ on cause, which is what 'central difference' in a paired impact/eruption set means, while A and D have them agreeing on cause.

15.why: B is illegal as support for a skeptic: a dose-response pattern strengthens the advantage claim it doubts. D is the only finding that explains away the positive literature; A and C remain arguable.

16.why: A and D are illegal for a 'weaken' stem because both report the cloud increase tracking the cooling, which strengthens the mechanism; B dissociates cooling from cloud formation and C bears on a different mechanism, so both remain legal.

17.why: A is the single middle position in a set whose other members are the two extremes (abandon the rules, revere them) plus a neutral history; a source-holder could still defend any of them.

18.why: A ('cannot be carried at all') and C ('every overtone ... nothing sacrificed') are mutually contradictory absolutes and an inference stem cannot key either; B and D both remain arguable, and B is the weaker, safer inference.

19.why: A is illegal because denying that transpiration cools 'at all' contradicts the physical premise any paired tree-cooling text shares; B is the conditional reply that answers a confident final sentence, while C and D remain arguable.

20.why: D is illegal: a pair of texts about a settlement's fate cannot have Text 2 denying the abandonment that gives both texts their subject. A is the only option in which the two texts stand in a layered relationship rather than flat denial or agreement.

21.why: B is illegal on its absolute ('always ... than any reliable account could achieve'), which no purpose statement would key; A is the only qualifying move, while C and D remain arguable.

22.why: B is illegal because it names compulsory schooling the 'sole cause' while conceding the press came centuries earlier, a claim no purpose statement carries; A is the enabling/causing distinction the other options orbit, and C and D remain arguable.

23.why: Four unrelated characterizations with no internal contradiction or corroboration among them; D chosen only because 'genuine prediction' is the term most often set against a post-hoc accommodation.

24.why: All four attitude pairs are legal for an unseen paragraph; D chosen only because it is the one pair not sharing the unease of the other three.
